content.title: About
content.content: Red salsa is a spicy sauce made from ripe tomatoes, red peppers, onion, garlic, vinegar and spices. It has a bright, slightly hot flavor with hints of sweetness and acidity, perfect for Mexican dishes, snacks and grilled foods.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Traditionally salsa is prepared with fresh ingredients without cooking.
The red color comes from ripe red tomatoes and/or red chili peppers.
Salsa is often used as a low‑calorie alternative to richer sauces and dressings.
In Mexico salsa is served with almost every meal, from tacos to grilled fish.
There are many regional salsa variations that differ in heat level and spice blend.

items.title: Rich in lycopene
items.content: Tomatoes, the main ingredient, contain lycopene – a powerful antioxidant that supports heart health and skin.

items.title: Vitamins C and A
items.content: Salsa provides vitamin C for immunity and vitamin A for vision.

items.title: Low‑calorie
items.content: One tablespoon of salsa contains about 10–15 kcal, making it a good choice for weight management.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Capsaicin from red peppers stimulates gastric secretions and may aid digestion.

items.title: Probiotic content
items.content: Fermented salsa can contain beneficial bacteria that promote gut health.

items.title: Spiciness
items.content: High heat may irritate the stomach of people with sensitive digestive systems.

items.title: Tomato allergy
items.content: Some individuals are allergic to tomatoes or peppers, which can cause skin or gastrointestinal reactions.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Salsa often contains added salt; those monitoring sodium intake should choose low‑salt versions.

items.title: Preservatives in commercial versions
items.content: Store‑bought salsa may contain preservatives and sweeteners that are not suitable for everyone.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Use salsa as a dip for chips, veggie sticks, shrimp, and as a topping for tacos, burritos, grilled meat, fish or chicken. It can be added to marinades, salads, or used as a base for soups.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep salsa in a tightly sealed jar in the refrigerator. Once opened, it lasts 1–2 weeks. Discard if it develops off‑odors or changes color.
